answer.evidence: The whole piece is drawn face-on. Rows 1-5 are a white header strip, the same near-white as the shelf-board fronts at rows 16-17 and 27-28. Rows 6-7 are a thin tan edge line with no eave shadow, so they read as a flat panel and not a receding top. Below, four cubbies show back walls (rows 8-15 and 19-26) and shoes drawn in side profile. The shelf lines at rows 18 and 29 are 1-2 row edges, and no band reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. The silhouette is a uniform 30 columns wide with a dark outline, and no side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are healthy: 17 visible tones per tile matches the cheese stall (17) and sits near the well (20), and near-flat coverage is 0%. The weakness is the outline. 100% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, and in the image the cabinet frame has a uniform grey-black line around it and around the shelf compartments. The references that carry tinted edges (hedge 0%, stall 1%) use dark material tones, so this reads as the 'sticker' outline. The only neutral reference is the iron lamp pole, where a neutral dark is natural for the material. The cream frame and shelf panels have only about 3-4 lightness steps, with little grain or per-plank shading, and look flatter than the stall's wood and awning ramps. The shoes add small colour clusters with some internal shading, which is why density is only slightly lower. Overall the piece is shallower than the Beodeul standard in outline treatment and material ramps.

answer.evidence: The unit is a flat face-on grid of two columns by two cubbies with side-view shoes inside. The white band at rows 1-5 is the same white as the side and bottom frame and carries tan smudges, so it reads as a header board or frame. Rows 6-7 (L=188, 165) are a divider line, and the same pair repeats at rows 18-19 as the mid-shelf, so it is not a distinct top-edge line. The only dark rows are inside the cubbies (row 8 at x=8 and x=23). There is no ellipse, no roof plane and no visible contents seen from above, so no horizontal top surface is drawn. The whole body is a vertical front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a shoe display wall: a pale cream/white frame with shelves holding small red, brown and blue shoes. On the measured facts it matches the references: 17 visible tones per tile (stall-cheese 17, well 20), 0% near-flat coverage. But 100% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line, and the references' tinted outlines (hedge 0%, stall 1%) are the Beodeul norm. The frame and back panel have only about 3 lightness steps (cream, light grey, dark grey) against 5-6 on the references' wood, roof and leaf ramps. Texture is limited to the shoe details; the cream panels are mostly smooth with little grain or speckle. The shoes carry some highlight and shadow variation, but the structure reads as a clean, slightly sticker-like panel rather than the layered, tinted shading of the stall or well. The neutral outline and shallow ramps on the main material outweigh the good tone count.
